intervals.label: NUSEX installation planned
intervals.note: Year precision. A 1980 communication says the apparatus will be installed in the tunnel; the laboratory's own founding date was not found, so this interval (the preparation of the first documented experiment) opens the facility record. Data taking in fact began on 1 June 1982.
intervals.quote: The NUSEX apparatus will be installed in the Mont Blanc Tunnel and the data taking is expected to start in the middle of 1981.

intervals.label: hosting NUSEX
intervals.note: Start is the start of NUSEX data taking (the first experiment documented here); the laboratory's own founding date was not found. No source consulted gives the laboratory's later history or closure, so the interval is left open and its present status is unknown. The quote is the OCR text layer of the NASA NTRS scan, which reads 'It has been running since June 1st, 1982 in a cave aside the Mont Blanc Tunnel'.
intervals.quote: June 1st, 1982 In a cave aside the Mont Blanc Tunnel

name: Mont Blanc Laboratory
notes: Other experiments are known to have used the laboratory (for example the Liquid Scintillation Detector, running from October 1984 according to a 1985 ICRC paper found in a search) but were not researched here; the record is the minimal facility NUSEX needs.
Status 'active' reflects only the open interval; whether the laboratory still operates was not established.

summary.plain: An underground laboratory in a cave beside the Mont Blanc road tunnel between France and Italy, under about five thousand metres of water-equivalent rock. Its first documented experiment was NUSEX, a 150-ton detector that looked for proton decay from 1982.
summary.technical: Cave laboratory half way along the Mont Blanc road tunnel at about 5000 m.w.e.; host of NUSEX (1982-) and later experiments. Founding date, operator and later history not established.
